question: Why do we run NGSadmix 20 times with 20 different seeds?

answers.answer: The likelihood surface can have local optima, so a single run started from a random guess may stop at a solution that is not the best one
answers.feedback: Correct. The seed decides the random starting point, and different starting points can end in different places.

answers.answer: To get 20 independent estimates that we can average
answers.feedback: No - and averaging would not even be possible: the K clusters come out in an arbitrary order, so column 1 of one run is not the same ancestral population as column 1 of another.

answers.answer: Because NGSadmix is stochastic and gives a different answer every time no matter what
answers.feedback: Not quite. With the same seed you get the same answer, and if the optimisation converges well all seeds give essentially the same answer.

question: You have the 20 log likelihoods in front of you. Which run do you use?

answers.answer: The one with the highest log likelihood
answers.feedback: Correct - that is our best shot at the maximum likelihood estimate.

answers.answer: The one with the lowest log likelihood
answers.feedback: No - we are maximising the likelihood. Remember these are negative numbers, so 'highest' means closest to zero.

answers.answer: The one whose plot looks most like what you expected
answers.feedback: Tempting, but that is choosing the answer before doing the analysis. Use the likelihood.

question: 19 of the 20 runs end at the same log likelihood and one ends clearly lower. What does that tell you?

answers.answer: The optimisation has most likely converged to the global maximum, and the odd run got stuck in a local optimum
answers.feedback: Correct. Many seeds reaching the same top value is the practical evidence of convergence we have.

answers.answer: That the data does not fit the admixture model
answers.feedback: Convergence and model fit are two different questions. evalAdmix, later in the exercise, is what tells you about fit.
Not from the likelihoods of a single K. You cannot see that here.
